name: Claude
look: Warm cream canvas with slab-serif display, a coral accent used scarcely on buttons and generously on callout bands.

hero.title: AI research and products that put safety first
hero.sub: Lumen is a model built to be useful, honest and harmless — and an assistant that says when it does not know something rather than inventing an answer.

features.title: A model you can hand real work to
features.sub: Long documents, messy codebases and questions where being wrong quietly would be expensive.

items.title: 200k of context
items.body: A whole codebase, a full contract set, or a year of meeting notes — held in one conversation without chunking.

items.title: Writes real code
items.body: Multi-file changes with the reasoning shown, and a willingness to say a plan is wrong before writing it.

items.title: Calibrated
items.body: Trained to express uncertainty rather than assert fluently. It will tell you when it is guessing.

items.title: Safety as design
items.body: Constitutional training rather than a filter bolted on afterwards, with the principles published.

items.title: Tools and MCP
items.body: Calls your functions, reads your systems, and connects to services through an open protocol.

items.title: Your data is yours
items.body: API inputs and outputs are not used for training. Zero-retention is available on request.

showcases.title: Deployed where the stakes are real
showcases.body: Legal review, clinical documentation and financial analysis — settings where a confident wrong answer costs more than no answer at all. Calibration is the feature that matters most, and it is the one we optimise hardest for.

showcases.title: We publish the uncomfortable results too
showcases.body: Interpretability work, evaluations where the model does badly, and the reasoning behind the safety framework. Where our results are weaker than a competitor's, that is in the paper as well.

gallery.title: Documentation
gallery.sub: Quickstarts, the API reference, prompt guidance and the tool-use protocol.

testimonial.quote: It told us our proposed schema had a problem before writing any of it. Every other assistant we trialled cheerfully wrote the broken version and let us find out in review.
testimonial.name: Marcus Owens

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.sub: Free to try. Pay per token on the API, or per seat for teams.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.desc: For trying Lumen on real work.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.desc: For people using it every day.

items.q: Do you train on my data?
items.a: Not on API inputs or outputs. Consumer conversations are used to improve the product unless you opt out, and the setting is in preferences rather than buried in a policy page.

items.q: What is the context window really?
items.a: 200,000 tokens, roughly 500 pages, and it holds across the whole conversation rather than degrading after the first few exchanges.
Through constitutional training — the model is trained against a published set of principles, rather than having a filter applied to its output afterwards. The principles are public.

items.q: Can it browse or run code?
items.a: It can call tools you define, including search and code execution, through an open protocol. Nothing runs unless you have wired it up and permitted it.

cta.title: Start with a real task
cta.sub: Free to try, no card. Give it something you would otherwise put off.

footer.tagline: AI research and products that put safety first.

notes: The warm cream canvas with warm dark ink is the defining choice. Pure white would make this a different brand entirely.
Coral is used scarcely on individual buttons but generously on full-bleed callout cards — two very different doses of the same accent.
Slab-serif display at weight 400 with negative tracking, paired with a humanist sans body. That pairing is the literary editorial voice.
Product mockups are dark navy cards carrying real code blocks and terminal panels — the brand shows product chrome rather than abstract illustration.
Radius is hierarchical: 8px for buttons and inputs, 12px for content cards, 16px for the hero container, pill for badges.
